title: Cross-Loop Query Handoff: How Later Loops Redirect Two-Hop Retrieval in the Ouro Looped Language Models
comment: Code and reproducibility: https://github.com/Muuzzziiy/cql-handoff 16 pages, 1 figure, 7 tables
summary: How do later loops in a pretrained looped language model repair two-hop retrieval? We study Ouro-1.4B and Ouro-2.6B by transplanting attention queries between loops at the same layer, head and final prompt position. On synthetic in-context questions, injecting the layer-indexed collection of loop-3 queries throughout loop 1 rescues 90% and 97% of questions answered incorrectly at loop 1 and correctly at loop 3, versus 24% and 21% for shuffled donors. The rescue also holds under greedy generation in Ouro-2.6B; in Ouro-1.4B it is limited to four-candidate ranking. Crossed donor-recipient swaps favor retrieval through the donor's bridge entity over copying its answer, although a substantial positional component remains in Ouro-2.6B. Late keys and values rescue far fewer targets. Freezing queries at their loop-1 values also damages two-hop accuracy more than a matched question that supplies the bridge. On natural questions, rescue is smaller and replicates only in Ouro-2.6B, and crossed swaps do not establish bridge redirection. These results identify a transferable collection of late-loop queries that supports bridge-conditioned retrieval on synthetic scenes; they do not locate where the bridge is computed or establish a single-vector handoff.

AI.brief_summary: 该文以 Ouro-1.4B/2.6B 循环语言模型为对象，在同层、同头、同末尾提示位置于不同 loop 间移植 attention query，考察后段循环如何修复合成情境下的两跳检索；发现把 loop-3 的 query 集合注入 loop 1 能挽救约九成错误样本，而晚期 key/value 效果明显更弱。
AI.relevance_reason: 这是纯文本循环模型的机制干预研究，不直接涉及视觉输入，但其「哪一循环的 query 携带可迁移的检索重定向信息」可供核查 LVR 中 loop 式状态更新、跨迭代信息贡献分配与注意力结构的作用。

title: Beyond Deduplication: Sharp Retrieval Limits for Attention with Correlated Distractors
summary: Redundant context affects attention through two distinct mechanisms: repeated items add normalization mass, while score variation within correlated groups can produce extreme individual scores. We separate these effects in a planted retrieval model with exponentially many Gaussian distractors arranged in known, exponentially large clusters. The model is a two-level generalized random energy model, whose classical free energy yields exact retrieval thresholds. Gaussian interpolation further shows that increasing positive correlation at fixed token count lowers the distractor free energy, unlike adding duplicates. Our main result identifies a sharp limitation of subtracting log cluster size from pre-softmax scores: this correction removes multiplicity but retains within-cluster extremes. Even a temperature chosen after observing all scores cannot lower the required signal below $\sqrt{2α_1}$, where $α_1$ is the exponential rate of the number of clusters. Averaging scores before exponentiation instead suppresses these fluctuations and achieves $\sqrt{2ρα_1}$, where $ρ$ is the within-cluster correlation. The gap persists after adding exponentially many singleton distractors, so group size alone does not identify the target, and extends to fixed finite hierarchies of light-tailed independent-increment scores. Finite-sample, stability, and participation results complement the asymptotic analysis. A controlled retrieval experiment with frozen sentence embeddings supports this distinction while delineating its scope: averaging helps when the relevant item is a singleton, but can discard useful evidence when a relevant group contains multiple matching items.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在带相关高斯干扰项的植入检索模型中分析 attention 的检索阈值，区分重复项的归一化效应与相关簇内的分数极值，并比较减去簇大小对数与先平均分数再指数的修正效果。
AI.relevance_reason: 其相关干扰组、组内证据聚合与检索极限分析，可能为 LVR 的视觉证据筛选和注意力检索结构提供理论线索；但冻结句向量实验能否迁移到多模态情形仍需核查。

title: SearchHorizonBench: A Benchmark for Search Value in AI Agents
summary: AI agents must decide when another search is worth its cost. Answer-success probabilities capture question difficulty, while this decision requires estimating the additional benefit of search. We introduce SearchHorizonBench, a benchmark for learning and evaluating search value from execution experience. Paired continuations and repeated executions separate expected search gain from generation noise and connect prediction quality to decision utility. The resource contains 45,632 executions across 3,168 questions. On 1,632 held-out questions, historical calibration reduces Brier error by 16.2%, with the improvement concentrated in success-level information. Search gains have a standard deviation of 21.4 percentage points, and tested historical estimators explain less than 2% of this variance in point estimates. Matched-configuration learning curves probe this distinction across training scales. At the reference token price, free selection observations yield a 2.49-point utility opportunity over the best constant action, driven primarily by gain information. Reusable histories, frozen splits, strong baselines and scoring tools provide a common foundation for developing and evaluating value-aware search agents.

AI.brief_summary: 该工作构建 SearchHorizonBench，用 3,168 个问题、45,632 次执行及配对续写来区分「再进行一次搜索的期望收益」与生成噪声，并考察收益预测质量如何转化为决策效用。
AI.relevance_reason: 其把「额外一步计算的边际收益」与停止决策效用显式分离并量化的做法，可能可供核查 LVR 中 THINK/LOOK/STOP 的停止判据与成本收益评估；能否迁移到多模态视觉证据获取尚需阅读原文。

title: Streaming Recurrent Memory
summary: Natural intelligence learns from a continuous stream of sensorimotor experience: data can arrive at high bandwidth, and behavior adapts to feedback as soon as it arrives, even when it is delayed. In contrast, most modern deep learning systems rely on stored datasets, replay buffers, and retained contexts through which credit is later assigned. At high data rates, storing and revisiting past experience can be impractical under tight memory and computational constraints. This paper studies recurrent memory under a streaming learning constraint: the learner learns from experience as soon as it arrives without storing raw experience. We ask whether a streaming learner can maintain a state that remains useful for future prediction and control from delayed feedback. We introduce Streaming Recurrent Memory (SRM), a recurrent memory designed for the streaming setting which preserves information that may matter later while remaining trainable with one-step backpropagation through time (BPTT). SRM provides a streaming-compatible recurrence that is designed to recall past information by content or time, track elapsed steps, and compose transformations whose outcome depends on the order in which inputs are observed. Across controlled memory tasks and streaming applications, SRM learns effectively with one-step BPTT, outperforming recurrent baselines in associative recall and online language modeling while achieving near-perfect success in associative T-Maze with delayed rewards. These results suggest that fixing how inputs are stored in the recurrent state, while learning how that state is read out, enables effective streaming learning without long-range backpropagation.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Streaming Recurrent Memory（SRM），在不能存储原始经验的流式设定下设计循环记忆状态，使其可按内容或时间回忆、跟踪步数并组合顺序相关变换，且仅用一步 BPTT 训练。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「固定写入状态、学习读出」及延迟反馈下维持可用状态的做法，可能为 LVR 的潜在状态维护、轨迹训练与信用分配提供可核查线索，但论文本身并非视觉或多模态工作。

title: Stop or Clarify? Experience-Conditioned Active Fact Verification
summary: Fact-verification benchmarks score the final label, while an interactive verifier must first decide whether the available evidence is sufficient. We focus on that intermediate Stop-or-Clarify Decision. Uncertainty alone is insufficient, because the benefit of another evidence-acquisition step is unknown before the step is taken. Sequential Experience-Adaptive Clarification (SEAC) wraps a fixed verifier with a lightweight evidence-acquisition policy. For each claim, SEAC retrieves evidence, runs the verifier, forms a label-free decision state, and combines stop risk with an observational clarification-utility estimate from earlier executed trajectories. Clarification is requested only when this score exceeds the action cost and decision threshold. On SciFact, LIAR, and FEVER, SEAC improves mean accuracy and macro-F1 over the compared fact-verification and active-retrieval baselines. Equal-budget and formula-level diagnostics support selective clarification as a contributor to the gain, while the small SciFact split leaves its paired improvement inconclusive.

AI.brief_summary: 研究交互式事实核查中的「停止或澄清」决策，提出 SEAC 在固定验证器外包裹轻量证据获取策略：由无标签决策状态结合停止风险与历史轨迹中的澄清效用估计，仅在得分超过动作成本与阈值时继续检索。
AI.relevance_reason: 其经验条件化的澄清效用估计与成本—阈值权衡，可为 LVR 中 LOOK/STOP 的收益成本判断和停止策略提供可核查线索；但工作属纯文本事实核查，未涉及视觉状态表示。

title: More Memory, Better Videos? A Controlled Study of Visual Memory in Long-Video Generation
summary: Long-video generators increasingly retrieve past visual observations to prevent identity drift. The intuition is compelling: more access to history should make future video more consistent. But an image can be faithful to the past and wrong for the present. Does visual memory always improve the generated story? We investigate this question through VMem-Bench, a two-track diagnostic study. Track-A measures which references are selected from 92 real films (16,548 segments), before generation and without generator confounds. Track-B compares four retrieval policies with no-memory and gold-informed last-seen controls on 30 causally generated stories (2,824 segments) using a shared generator. Retrieval increases entity recall from 0.559 to 0.628-0.693 and improves similarity to past appearances, but decreases precision from 0.977 to 0.915-0.938 and forbidden-entity avoidance from 0.968 to 0.845-0.898. It can also reinforce obsolete appearances after the story changes them. Conversely, high long-gap recall can arise without memory when the prompt itself supplies the appearance; an appearance-stripping analysis exposes this confound. These results distinguish historical fidelity from current-story correctness and show why retrieval relevance or final-video consistency alone does not establish memory utility.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 VMem-Bench，用双轨诊断研究长视频生成中的视觉记忆检索：在 92 部真实影片上测量参考选择，并在共享生成器下比较四种检索策略与无记忆、给定答案的对照，考察检索对实体召回、精度和禁止实体规避的影响。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「检索相关性或最终一致性不等于记忆有用」的结论与剥离外观线索的混淆分析，可供核查 LVR 中视觉证据是否被真正使用，以及历史保真与当前任务正确性的区分。

title: When Pointing Becomes Profiling: Social Bias and Refusal in Text-Steerable Visual Encoders
summary: Text-steerable visual encoders condition a frozen Vision Transformer on a natural-language prompt and point at the matching image region, producing prompt-conditioned heatmaps and features. We audit the released SteerViT model and find that its steering interface turns language-driven pointing into demographic profiling. On counterfactual face mosaics and real multi-person photographs, "the person" selects a man more often than the base rate, crime words select Black people more often than occupation words do, "the man" among four women selects the Black woman 75.6% of the time on SocialCounterfactuals, and "the monkey" selects Black people. None of them is in the backbone's unsteered saliency, and the crime association is not in the frozen text encoder; the race effects grow with steering strength and enter through the last two cross-attention layers: giving the prompt to those layers alone reproduces them. Four other grounding models, CLIPSeg, Grounding-DINO, SAM 3, and Qwen2.5-VL, show no crime routing and weaker race routing. The model cannot refuse. Its patch softmax must place its mass somewhere, and its heatmap separates a groundable request ("the police officer") from one that is absent ("the pizza") or that would require a stereotyped demographic inference ("the criminal") only at chance (AUROC 0.52). We introduce SafeSteer, which adds a learned abstention output and counterfactual-invariance training on the same 23M steering parameters. SafeSteer separates should-point from should-abstain prompts at AUROC 0.997, generalizes to held-out sensitive and absent words (0.998; at a 0.5 threshold it refuses 99.8% of trained and 62% of held-out sensitive words) with no over-refusal of visible people on the benchmark, and removes most race routing while keeping localization and retrieval within 1 point of the released model. Code, benchmarks, and the curated mosaic sets will be released.

AI.brief_summary: 论文审计文本可引导视觉编码器 SteerViT，发现其指向接口会把语言定位变成人口统计画像且无法拒答，并提出 SafeSteer，加入学习式弃答输出与反事实不变训练。
AI.relevance_reason: 「应指向 vs 应弃答」的 abstention 头与反事实不变训练，可能为 LVR 的视觉证据筛选与 STOP 决策提供监督线索；偏差经最后两层 cross-attention 注入，也供核查证据进入内部状态的位置。

title: Reinforcement Learning Done Right for Explicit Confidence Targets
summary: Large language models (LLMs) can produce plausible but incorrect answers when they are uncertain, which can mislead users and undermine model reliability. Training models to abstain with reinforcement learning is a natural approach, but most existing methods use a fixed error penalty and therefore cannot adapt their behavior to different confidence requirements at inference time. We study \emph{explicit confidence targets}, where a user specifies a target \(p\) in the prompt and the model directly chooses whether to answer or abstain, with the goal of achieving an accuracy of at least \(p\) among answered questions. However, learning to respond to different confidence targets with a single model has proven difficult, and prior attempts have failed to distinguish different targets. We show that this failure comes from two problems: the reward signal that distinguishes different values of $p$ is often lost during optimization, while the original error penalty grows without bound as $p$ approaches one. We propose RLEC (\textbf{R}einforcement \textbf{L}earning with \textbf{E}xplicit \textbf{C}onfidence Targets), which preserves the learning signal needed to distinguish confidence targets, introduces a stable reward family that keeps the desired answer condition unchanged, and uses reward scheduling to balance effective learning and training stability. Together, these designs enable the first successful training of a single LLM for explicit confidence target control. Extensive experiments across diverse benchmarks and model scales show that RLEC largely preserves general capabilities and achieves competitive calibration performance. RLEC also supports fine-grained target control without an external decision system or threshold calibration after training. By making explicit confidence targets part of the trained policy, RLEC opens a new and more direct path toward behavioral calibration.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究「显式置信目标」设置：用户在 prompt 中给定目标 p，模型自行决定作答或弃答，使已答题目的准确率不低于 p；作者指出单一模型难以区分不同 p 的原因在于区分 p 的奖励信号在优化中丢失、且错误惩罚在 p 趋于 1 时无界增长，据此提出 RLEC，用保持作答条件不变的稳定奖励族与奖励调度完成单模型训练。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「按目标置信度决定作答或弃答」的策略训练与奖励整形，可供核查 LVR 中 STOP 决策如何受目标条件驱动、以及停止阈值难以随目标变化的失败模式是否同源；但该方法目前针对纯文本单步弃答，迁移到多步视觉证据获取与 latent 状态需另行判断。

title: From Denoising Dynamics to Endpoint Uncertainty in Diffusion Language Models
summary: Predictive uncertainty in stochastic language-model inference can be characterized by repeatedly sampling an input and measuring the distribution of outputs. This requires multiple complete generations. Masked diffusion language models expose another source of information: the evolution of the output during denoising. We ask whether convergence within diffusion trajectories is associated with uncertainty across their final outputs, or endpoints. We study four masked diffusion language models on four reasoning benchmarks, collecting 20 generations per question and 32,000 denoising trajectories in total. Within each trajectory, we measure within-run concentration as the area under the curve describing stable resolution of the eventual output. Across repeated trajectories, we measure endpoint-distribution uncertainty. Stronger within-run concentration is associated with lower endpoint entropy after accounting for model and dataset ($β=-0.222$, $p<10^{-25}$). This association persists for multi-token outputs and when reweighting positive-entropy cases. The relationship is asymmetric: high within-run concentration almost exclusively accompanies concentrated endpoint distributions, whereas lower concentration occurs under both concentrated and competing endpoint regimes. This relationship strengthens as denoising proceeds. Features from a single denoising run predict whether independent held-out runs will concentrate on a common endpoint or produce competing endpoints. These results connect dynamics within individual denoising runs to variability across repeated inference. Within-trajectory dynamics contain information about whether independent repetitions will concentrate on a common endpoint or produce competing endpoints, providing a route towards estimating endpoint-distribution properties with fewer complete generations.

AI.brief_summary: 在四个 masked diffusion language model 与四个推理基准上共采集 32,000 条去噪轨迹，检验单次轨迹内输出收敛程度与重复采样终点分布不确定性之间的关系，发现二者负相关且不对称，并可用单条轨迹特征预测独立运行是否集中到同一终点。
AI.relevance_reason: 纯文本 diffusion 推理工作，但其用轨迹内收敛度估计重复采样不确定性的做法，可能为 LVR 中 latent 状态收敛判断、停止决策与动态计算预算提供可核查的线索。

title: Free to Look, Free to Reason: Simple LLM Harnesses Outdiagnose Hand-Crafted Root Cause Analysis Agents
summary: Root cause analysis (RCA) of microservice failures has attracted many LLM agents whose investigation is hand-crafted, through standard operating procedures, fixed stages and role agents. Each is evaluated on its own data against few baselines, so it is unknown whether this design beats letting a capable model investigate on its own. We compare three simple harnesses that prescribe none of the model's calls (one call over an evidence package, a SQL agent and the Codex coding agent) with five published LLM RCA agents and with statistical and causal methods on RCAtlas, 90 validated cases from eight public datasets, across six models and three reasoning efforts. The simple harnesses are the most accurate (PR@1 65-77% on three mid-tier models), ahead of the published agents (16-53%) and the non-LLM methods (6-39%), on every model on which both families were run. The published agents fix from a tenth to all of their model calls in the program, and a case study shows how these prescriptions skip the decisive evidence. A stronger model mainly improves reliability, a multi-turn harness mainly improves aptitude, and more reasoning effort changes accuracy by a few points at most while multiplying the time by up to seven. Among runs more accurate than the best non-LLM method, every Pareto-optimal run in cost or time uses a simple harness.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在 90 个经校验的微服务故障案例上，比较三种不预设模型调用的简单 harness（单次调用证据包、SQL agent、Codex 编码 agent）与五个已发表 LLM RCA agent 及统计/因果方法，并考察模型强度、多轮与推理努力对准确率和耗时的影响。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「固定阶段与角色预设会跳过决定性证据」以及「提高推理努力只换来数个百分点却成倍增加时间」的结论，可能为 LVR 中 LOOK/STOP 决策与推理预算分配提供可核查的对照线索，但属非视觉的文本 RCA 设定，迁移需进一步判断。

title: FOCUS: Active Critic Learning for Long-Horizon Language Model Agents
summary: Sparse outcome rewards make it difficult for long-horizon language-model agents to assign credit to earlier actions. Learned critics provide value estimates for intermediate states, but these estimates can be inaccurate, while estimating intermediate values with repetitive continuation samples from points within a trajectory incurs substantial costs. To mitigate these issues, we introduce FOCUS, an RL method that uses selective branching to help the critic network learn its value estimator. The rollout controller facilitates active learning for the critic by sampling continuations from states that are expected to most reduce the critic's estimation error. These refined value estimates then score the segment between consecutive states with a TD($λ$) advantage, while the sampled evidence supplies training targets for the critic. FOCUS supports long-horizon agentic reinforcement learning through a modular context-management interface that decouples context management from rollout allocation. Our experiments show that using compaction-induced segment boundaries for value estimation and credit assignment, FOCUS outperforms GRPO and VinePPO with matched per-step generation budgets on legal reasoning, deep search, and code localization benchmarks, improving held-out accuracy at Qwen3.5-9B scale by 7.2 points over the strongest baseline on BrowseComp-Plus (55.4 vs. 48.2) and by 4.1 points on DeonticBench (56.5 vs. 52.4).

AI.brief_summary: 提出 FOCUS，一种面向长时程语言模型智能体的 RL 方法：用选择性分支从最可能降低 critic 估值误差的状态处采样续写，再以 TD(λ) 优势在压缩片段间完成信用分配，在深度检索、法律推理与代码定位基准上优于 GRPO 和 VinePPO。
AI.relevance_reason: 其按估值误差主动分配续写预算、并用片段级优势打分来定位关键步骤的思路，可供核查 LVR 中的贡献分配、轨迹监督与分支/停止决策，但论文是纯文本智能体工作，未涉及视觉证据与 latent 状态生成。

title: Does VGGT Know What It Does Not Know?
summary: Feed-forward 3D reconstruction models such as VGGT regress cameras and geometry in a single forward pass, but they report no uncertainty for the camera poses they predict: an incorrect relative pose looks no different from a correct one. We ask whether the frozen model nonetheless knows when its pose is wrong. On HardMatch, a benchmark of 1,000 deliberately difficult image pairs on which VGGT fails on 35% of pairs, a linear probe on VGGT's frozen features predicts pose failure on held-out categories with ROC-AUC 93.5%, compared with 79.7% for VGGT's own point-map confidence and 77.7% for a classifier trained on all of VGGT's outputs. The probe catches failures VGGT is confident about, lets a downstream system abstain on the pairs it distrusts, and transfers without retraining to rotation failures on PhotoTourism and ScanNet-1500, beyond what co-visibility explains. This knowledge is absent from the per-image encoder: it is computed partway through the layers that fuse the two views, and the same holds for a second model, $π^3$. In essence, we find that VGGT knows more about its own failures than it reports.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究冻结的 VGGT 是否在内部特征中编码相机位姿失败：用线性探针预测失败，比较点图置信度与输出分类器，并定位到双视图融合层，同时验证弃权与跨数据集迁移。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「从冻结内部特征读取失败信号并定位计算层」的探针方法，可供核查 LVR 中 latent 是否携带可靠性证据、能否据此停止或弃权；但对象是 3D 重建而非 VLM 推理。

title: GRASP: Group-Adaptive Hybrid RL-SFT Post-Training for Medical VQA without Reasoning Annotations
summary: Adapting general-purpose vision-language models (VLMs) to medical visual question answering (VQA) is valuable for helping clinicians read images and make diagnoses, but annotated data are scarce and provide only short answers, without reasoning annotations. Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) fits these labels but overfits to them and amplifies their biases, eroding out-of-domain (OOD) generalization. Reinforcement learning (RL) better preserves generalization but never uses the gold answer as a training target: GRPO-style algorithms learn from the contrast between correct and incorrect answers within a group of sampled responses, so all-correct or all-wrong groups give no correctness signal. Existing SFT-RL hybrids either apply SFT and RL in separate stages or switch between them per question, or need reasoning traces from experts or stronger models, which medical VQA data lack. We propose GRASP, which combines RL and SFT in every update using only short answers: RL lets the model explore its own reasoning, SFT teaches the gold answer after that reasoning to supply the direct supervision RL lacks, and their balance adapts to how well the model answers each question. Tuning only about 1% of the parameters with LoRA, GRASP outperforms all compared training objectives both in domain and on OOD open-ended questions across Qwen3-VL-8B, InternVL3-8B and Gemma 3-4B. On an OOD benchmark spanning eight imaging modalities, GRASP-trained InternVL3-8B and Qwen3-VL-8B beat all 10 compared general and medical VLMs in open-ended accuracy, including models trained on up to 2,600 times more data or with over 250 times more trainable parameters. We release MedTerse, a dataset of 12.9K short-answer questions, and our code at https://github.com/sea-comet/GRASP-MedVQA.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 GRASP，在每次参数更新中同时使用 RL 与 SFT：先让模型自行探索推理，再对金标短答案做直接监督，并按各题答题情况自适应调节二者权重，用于缺乏推理标注的医学 VQA 后训练，仅用 LoRA 调约 1% 参数。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「无推理轨迹、仅用短答案做轨迹级监督」与按题难度自适应分配探索/监督权重的设计，与 LVR 训练中的监督信号来源和贡献分配问题相关，可供核查；但不涉及 latent 状态生成或视觉证据内部机制。

title: EARS: Evidence-Aware Retrieval via Sound and Motion for Budgeted Video Reasoning
summary: Uniform frame sampling can miss brief evidence in sparse-event videos when the VLM sees only K frames. We propose EARS (Evidence-Aware Retrieval via Sound and motion), a training-free, query-free front-end that ranks frames using optical-flow motion and audio energy, then applies temporal non-maximum suppression for diversity. The evidence score alone has frame-level AP 0.39; used only to select frames for the VLM, EARS with temporal diversity reaches localization AP 0.94, compared with 0.88 under Uniform sampling. In the updated matched study, at K = 1 EARS reaches XD-subset F1 0.660 versus 0.614 for centered Uniform (the paired interval includes zero); earlier backbone studies use separate protocols. On mostly-silent UCF-Crime, however, EARS slightly trails Uniform. A single configuration is used across both benchmarks; the new controls do not repeat the original held-out search. EARS therefore targets low-budget videos whose salient evidence aligns with motion or audio; on dense narratives or stealthy events, uniform or semantic selection remains preferable, and cheap modality statistics cannot reliably route between them. title: Where Rounding Happens Matters: Rounding-Location Alignment Stabilizes LLM Reinforcement Learning
summary: Reinforcement learning for large language models often uses separate systems for inference and training. Even with identical weights and BF16 tensors, implementation differences can make an intended on-policy update off-policy and destabilize training. Existing remedies align the entire inference and training stacks, change global precision, or modify the learning algorithm. We ask whether aligning selected parts of the execution stack can stabilize BF16 RL while other implementation differences remain. We align training-side rounding locations with inference in three regions---RoPE, SwiGLU, and residual RMSNorm---by retaining selected intermediates in FP32 until their BF16 outputs. Across four Qwen-family models, aligning all three regions prevents the collapse observed under the default BF16 baseline; RoPE-path alignment alone also suffices in the studied runs, despite remaining numerical discrepancies. The interventions keep the inference engine, matrix-multiplication and attention kernels, and learning objective unchanged.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究 LLM 强化学习中推理栈与训练栈的 BF16 舍入位置不一致如何使本应在策略上的更新实际变成 off-policy 并导致训练崩溃；提出在 RoPE、SwiGLU 与残差 RMSNorm 三处保留 FP32 中间值直至其 BF16 输出，仅对齐这些局部舍入位置，在四个 Qwen 模型上即可避免默认 BF16 基线的崩溃。

title: Evolving to Match Capabilities: Improving Harness Self-Evolution via Skill Adaptation
summary: Harness self-evolution offers a practical route for LLM agents to improve from execution experience without updating model parameters. Its effectiveness depends on whether models can successfully act on the guidance provided by their harnesses. However, we find that harness benefits are not uniform across model capabilities: skills that improve stronger models can provide little benefit or even degrade performance for weaker ones. Across seven models and three benchmarks, we identify 103 task-skill pairs where skills improve GPT-5.6-luna by 31.1 points but degrade Gemma-4-E4B by 8.8 points. In 86% of failed weak-model runs, the violated requirement is already stated in the skill. This motivates skill adaptation: reformulating existing skills to match the executor's capabilities and make their guidance easier to execute. To achieve this, we diagnose failures in tool execution, context management, instruction following, and verification, and distill these diagnoses into a fixed meta-skill that guides adaptation during harness self-evolution. Guided by the meta-skill, a capable external rewriter, Kimi-K3, adapts skills without execution evidence, improving the three weak executors by 5.1-14.1 points over the original skills. We then incorporate this adaptation into a five-round self-evolution loop, where each model revises its own skill from execution trajectories and verifier feedback. Across seven executors, from Gemma-4-E4B to Kimi-K2.5, the meta-skill consistently improves final scores by 2.0-5.1 points over the same loop without the meta-skill. Our findings provide practical design guidance for developing more effective harness self-evolution methods.

title: Lessons from Luck: Do LLM-Written Lessons Carry Chance into an Agent's Next Decision?
comment: 28 pages, 1 figure, 11 tables. A registered study: the protocol, code and stimuli were frozen, deposited (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23253562) and timestamped in a Bitcoin block before the confirmatory run. The locked run records are public (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23272809)
summary: Self-improving agents write lessons from the outcomes of their runs; when outcomes are noisy, a lesson can carry chance into later decisions. We measure one link of this chain in a registered study. In 256 synthetic worlds, each a recurring task with two interchangeable tools of recorded reliability, a scripted previous run used the more reliable tool (a good decision) or the less reliable one (a bad decision), with an assigned outcome: success or a transient failure. A model wrote a lesson from the run with ReasoningBank's memory-writing instruction; a fresh session of the same model, holding the authoritative log and the previous result, chose the next run's first tool with one memory item: that lesson, the lesson from the other outcome, an irrelevant item, or an unreasoned directive. The protocol was frozen, deposited and timestamped before any confirmatory call; 11 LLM endpoints gave 90,084 answers. After a chance failure of the better tool, the panel's lessons carried the chance (registered reading luck-carrying; interaction +0.112, 95% interval [+0.097, +0.126]): readers named the worse tool in 11.6% of next runs with the lesson written from that failure, against 0.4% with an irrelevant item and 0.4% with the lesson written from a success. The effect was +0.042 where the log stated that failures are independent and +0.181 where it did not (descriptive). After a lucky success of the worse tool, the interaction was bounded below 0.10 (+0.002), a bound, not evidence of no harm. In exploratory readings, 6 endpoints carried the chance (up to +0.352); 5 were bounded below 0.10. In secondary comparisons, a three-sentence decision-quality note in the writing instruction lowered the worse-tool rate after a chance failure to 7.5%, and one instruction for both outcomes with a no-change option to 3.1%; neither met the registered harm-reduction rule at every such endpoint.

title: EKT-Router: Expert-Evidence Alignment for Embodied Vision-Language Models
summary: Embodied vision-language models must answer questions from partial, evolving observations. Their success depends on both the reasoning capability selected and the evidence available to it. Expert routers adapt internal computation, while tool-augmented systems acquire external evidence; choosing these independently can leave a suitable expert without the evidence it needs. We introduce EKT-Router, a bounded framework that jointly selects a capability expert, optional knowledge, and perceptual tools. Outcome-derived signatures represent the overlapping strengths of General, Spatial Reasoning, and Spatiotemporal experts. A joint utility scores complete expert-evidence routes under a call budget. After acquisition, a packet verifier admits valid evidence with positive predicted expert-conditioned gain. The selected expert then answers once, reverting to the unchanged observation if all packets are rejected. Across 6 embodied QA benchmarks, EKT-Router achieves a mean score of 61.4, the highest among the compared systems, and averages 74.7 on 10 general vision-language benchmarks. With all external evidence disabled, question-conditioned expert selection alone improves over the best fixed expert by 1.75 points. Ablations show that learned routing is the dominant component and that knowledge and perception are complementary.

title: MARC: Mechanism-Aware Reflective Correction for Articulated Object Code Generation
summary: Generating an articulated object from images and text requires more than plausible parts and movable joints: the assembled mechanism must execute the intended motion. This is particularly challenging for closed-chain and coupled mechanisms, where an error in one connection can block motion or separate connected parts. We introduce MARC, Mechanism-Aware Reflective Correction, which shares an executable kinematic graph across program construction, motion solving, and correction. The graph binds physical connections to local attachment frames and represents loop closures and joint-coordinate couplings. Given prescribed driver inputs, a numerical solver computes follower motion and associates errors with specific connections and configurations. The agent uses these diagnostics to probe possible causes, revise connections or geometry, and retest the mechanism along the original motion paths. On a 20-object test set, MARC with Kimi-K3 achieves 67.8% valid motion coverage and 60.0% overall success, outperforming six baselines. Starting from the same initial candidates, correction improves these scores by 13.7 and 20.0 percentage points, respectively. Ablations further show the benefits of graph-based mechanism support and graph-guided repair. Project homepage: https://demianmusk.github.io/MARC-Home/.

title: A Canary in the Neural Mine: Catching an Image Classifier's Silent, Confident Failures
summary: Deployed vision models auto-accept confident predictions, so high-confidence errors propagate silently. Maximum Softmax Probability (MSP), the standard failure predictor, has a structural blind spot: as a scalar read from the classifier head, it is first-order blind to feature variation orthogonal to its confidence gradient. Through a factorial analysis of feature-space detectors, we identify a conditional-redundancy principle explaining why they fail to complement MSP: the class-separability geometry they measure is already encoded in MSP and collapses under fusion. The signal that survives is class-conditional typicality on the off-manifold residual---and because this residual's distribution varies by backbone, from near-Gaussian to heavy-tailed, it must be estimated non-parametrically. We instantiate these findings as CANARY, a training-free detector that computes a per-class kNN distance on the PCA residual of the penultimate feature, percentile-calibrates it on validation data, and fuses it with MSP through a single validation-tuned weight. CANARY's benefit follows a headroom law: gains grow as baseline MSP quality falls, so a single clean-validation number forecasts the improvement. With every parameter selected on in-distribution data alone, CANARY matches or improves 382 of 385 shift cells (e-AURC; 379 on AUROC) across five backbones, with worst-case regression within seed noise ($-0.0002$ AUROC) and the largest gains on natural distribution shifts (ImageNet-A/R, ObjectNet)---where deployed models are most exposed.

title: ProtoEEG: Structured Prototype Alignment for EEG Visual Decoding
summary: EEG visual decoding remains difficult because scalp recordings are noisy, spatially coarse, and variable across trials and subjects. Most systems align each trial with a dense image embedding, although that embedding mixes semantic content with instance-specific texture, pose, and background. This target can demand details absent from EEG and provides no explicit account of the visual factors supporting a prediction. We propose \textbf{ProtoEEG}, a prototype-mediated framework that reformulates EEG--image alignment as soft composition over a shared learnable visual codebook. A trainable EEG encoder and a frozen visual teacher produce assignment distributions over the same $K=64$ prototypes. Their weighted reconstructions form a structured representation for retrieval and image generation. Prototype contrast supplies the main cross-modal training signal, distribution alignment coordinates codebook use across modalities, an instance anchor preserves fine-grained discrimination, and diversity regularization prevents redundant prototypes. The shared assignment profile also makes the learned bottleneck directly testable through prototype retention, random selection, and identity shuffling. Across five seeds, ProtoEEG reaches 64.0\% Top-1 and 91.5\% Top-5 on THINGS-EEG2 200-way retrieval. After retraining on EEG-ImageNet, it obtains 44.8\% Top-1 and 73.8\% Top-5 in 80-way retrieval. ProtoEEG also ranks first on all seven reconstruction metrics. Removing prototype contrast lowers Top-1 by 56.9 percentage points, while shuffling prototype identities reduces it to 0.5\%. Prototype analyses further show distributed assignments and broad codebook use rather than one-prototype routing. These results support structured alignment targets as a practical alternative to increasing encoder or teacher capacity alone.

title: WorldCast: World-Consistent Character Video Generation with Large-Angle Camera Control
summary: Precise camera control is essential for cinematic character video generation, yet existing methods struggle to follow large-angle trajectories with combined rotation, translation, and radius variation from arbitrary initial azimuths. Such viewpoint changes also reveal character regions unseen in the initial frame, causing geometric distortions, appearance degradation, and identity drift. To systematically study these coupled challenges, we introduce CLACT, a large-scale Character-centric dataset and benchmark covering diverse Large-Angle Camera Trajectories, with accurate camera geometry and multi-view character observations for training and evaluation. We further propose WorldCast, a framework for world-consistent character video generation under diverse large-angle camera motions. Specifically, we back-project the initial frame into a 3D point cloud using estimated depth, align the point-cloud scale with the target camera trajectory, and render it along the trajectory to obtain explicit geometric guidance and coverage masks. To complement the incomplete character information, we introduce Geometry-Aligned Memory Attention (GAMA). Using relative camera poses estimated jointly from the initial frame and multi-view character anchors, we express anchor and target-view geometry in a common coordinate frame. GAMA uses this geometric alignment to guide the retrieval and injection of view-relevant character features during generation. Evaluations across diverse large-angle camera trajectories demonstrate accurate trajectory following while preserving character geometry, appearance, and identity.

title: Learning Pathology-Sensitive Representations for Unsupervised Retinal OCT Anomaly Detection
summary: Deep learning approaches for retinal optical coherence tomography (OCT) predominantly rely on predefined disease categories, limiting their ability to detect rare or previously unseen abnormalities. While visual foundation models provide transferable representations, their effectiveness in identifying pathological deviations from normal retinal anatomy remains insufficiently understood. In this work, we introduce an unsupervised framework for retinal OCT anomaly detection and localization that adapts pretrained visual representations to normal retinal anatomy through anatomy-aware reconstruction and contrastive triplet learning guided by synthetic structural perturbations, without requiring disease-specific annotations. We systematically investigate the influence of pretraining strategies, anatomy-aware representation adaptation, and anomaly scoring mechanisms on the detection and localization of unseen retinal abnormalities. Our findings demonstrate that adapting pretrained representations to normal retinal structure improves anomaly sensitivity, while pixel-space reconstruction errors and feature-space deviations provide complementary signals for identifying pathological changes. These findings underscore the importance of anatomy-aware representation learning and offer insights into developing generalizable retinal anomaly detection frameworks beyond predefined disease categories.

title: Support-guided OOD Removal with Diffusion
summary: Many real-world signals are corrupted by localized, structured perturbations whose distribution is unknown: an intermittent background noise in a music recording, a watermark stamped on a photograph, a cast shadow. We study the task of recovering a clean signal $x$ from an observation $y$ containing such a localized out-of-distribution (OOD) corruption. We propose Support-guided OOD Removal with Diffusion, SORD, an iterative algorithm to recover $x$ using only two ingredients: a binary map of the corruption support and a single diffusion model pretrained on clean signals. SORD does not require any paired data or any statistical model of the corruption. We evaluate SORD on natural images and human faces with spatially localized corruptions including handwritten digits, other images, watermarks, and shadows, as well as audio recordings of different musical instruments with temporally localized corruptions including other instruments and human speech. SORD is competitive with, and often outperforms, posterior-sampling inpainting given the same diffusion prior and the same mask, source-separation baselines that require a separate diffusion model for each source, and, on several benchmarks, supervised networks trained on paired clean and corrupted signals. The code is released here: \href{https://github.com/voilalab/SORD}{https://github.com/voilalab/SORD}.

title: Neyman Orthogonal Activation Steering
summary: Activation steering is a popular approach for shifting LLM output toward a desired behavior, and increasingly for generating realistic synthetic data. The standard recipe estimates a steering direction by contrasting LLM activations on prompts with and without a target concept, such as truthfulness. In this paper, we separate the estimand (the steering direction these methods target) from the estimator used to recover it, two notions the literature often conflates. We frame nearly all existing methods as plug-in estimators of the average gradient of an outcome regression, with the binary contrastive label fixed as the outcome. Using this framing, we can immediately incorporate flexible modeling approaches and extend existing methods to allow for continuous outcomes such as log-probabilities or oracle ratings. Flexible ML models that fit the outcome well, however, might not estimate the gradient well, which motivates estimators that target the gradient directly. Drawing on the debiased machine learning literature, we develop a complementary estimator built on the Stein score, the Riesz representer of the gradient functional. Combining the two routes gives an orthogonalized estimator with classical double-robustness properties. We illustrate the framework on activation steering applied to a number of benchmark datasets.

AI.brief_summary: 论文把激活引导中的目标方向（estimand）与估计器区分开，将现有方法统一看作结果回归平均梯度的 plug-in 估计，并借去偏机器学习与 Stein score 提出正交化、具双稳健性质的方向估计器，在多个基准上演示。

title: Distilling Expert Judgment at Scale
summary: Frontier AI models are increasingly deployed on topics where the stakes are high and expert judgment is required, including healthcare, defense, finance, governance, and politics. We present a general methodology for distilling expert human judgment into automated evaluation systems that operate at scale. Our approach assembles networks of domain experts and develops techniques for extracting not just their conclusions but their reasoning processes, encoding those processes into structured editorial standards that automated judges can apply continuously. We ground our approach in a long tradition of research on the nature of expertise and the conditions under which expert judgment is reliable and more effective than other approaches, and argue that independent, expert-calibrated evaluation is necessary not only on epistemic grounds but as a matter of accountability and public trust. We validate the methodology on AI news reporting as a first application domain. On source quality, two independent domain experts achieve Krippendorff's $α= 0.83/0.69$ on a held-out test set when applying the editorial standards, and our automated judge reaches $F1 = 0.81/0.97$ against expert consensus. On neutrality, experts achieve $α= .72$ on the test set, and the automated judge reaches $F1 = 0.86$ against expert consensus. Additionally, a controlled comparison shows that expert-calibrated judges substantially outperform uncalibrated frontier models on every source-quality metric, demonstrating that encoding expert reasoning is the critical step that prompt engineering alone cannot replace. We present this benchmark as a proof of concept for a broader evaluation infrastructure applicable to any domain where judgment matters and expertise is scarce.

AI.brief_summary: 提出把领域专家判断蒸馏为可扩展自动评测系统的方法：组建专家网络，不仅提取结论还提取其推理过程，编码为结构化编辑标准供自动评审持续应用；在 AI 新闻报道的来源质量与中立性上报告专家间信度与自动评审 F1，并显示专家校准的评审优于未校准前沿模型。

title: AdaPRA: Process Reward Agents with Adaptive Rubrics for Data Science
summary: Data science agents can automate end-to-end machine learning workflows, yet they remain far from competitive on human leaderboards. Agents make process errors such as insufficient exploration, unsound validation, coding bugs, and poor use of a fixed budget (re-running the same exploratory data analysis and baseline models in every attempt). We propose AdaPRA to address these issues: a persistent coding agent harness that accumulates knowledge across attempts on the same task, with rubric-guided process supervision that identifies and corrects errors. Our process reward agent audits the agent's trajectory and workspace by executing checks, and adapts its rubrics to each task. We find that rubrics seeded from easier tasks generalize to harder tasks, with rubric adaptation further improving performance. With five attempts per task, AdaPRA improves an 80B Qwen model's leaderboard percentile by 24.5 points on DSPredict-Easy and 14.8 points on DSPredict-Hard while reducing process errors. We also show that supervision with rubrics mined from one base model's runs improves another (DeepSeek-V3.2), and that AdaPRA beats DataPRM, a competitive PRM for data science. We also share our code for reproducibility.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 AdaPRA，为数据科学智能体设计跨尝试累积知识的持久 coding harness，并用可自适应、通过执行检查审计轨迹与工作区的 rubric 过程奖励智能体来发现并纠正过程错误，在 DSPredict 上提升 80B Qwen 的名次百分位。

title: Scoped Semantic Invariance as a Foundation for LLM Reliability
summary:
LLMs often answer semantically equivalent queries inconsistently, even when the underlying facts are known. We formalize consistency as semantic invariance over equivalence classes of queries and show that invariance under arbitrary meaning-preserving transformations is undecidable in general. This motivates scoped semantic invariance, where model behavior is evaluated relative to bounded semantic domains.
  We operationalize this framework using knowledge graphs (KGs), which act as explicit semantic control structures defining local semantic constraints and grounding contexts. Across the MITRE D3FEND ontology and eight Wikidata- derived domains, we show that inconsistencies are structured rather than random, concentrating in localized hotspot subgraphs organized around recurring TREE, STAR, and CYCLE patterns that remain stable across models and domains.
  We further show that selective graph grounding improves correctness and cross-model consistency, while indiscriminate grounding introduces regressions. A layered grounding strategy achieves the strongest monotonicity profile, preserving correct knowledge while reducing inconsistency. Finally, we show that hotspot structures discovered from simple consistency probes transfer to more realistic compositional reasoning tasks.

AI.brief_summary: 论文把 LLM 对语义等价查询的一致性问题形式化为语义不变性，指出任意保义变换下的不变性不可判定，转而提出限定语义域内的 scoped semantic invariance，并以知识图谱作为语义控制结构，在 D3FEND 与八个 Wikidata 域上发现不一致集中于 TREE/STAR/CYCLE 型热点子图，且比较了选择性接地与无差别接地的效果。
AI.relevance_reason: 「选择性接地改善、无差别接地反而退步」可为视觉证据筛选与注入策略提供待核查的方法线索，热点子图诊断思路也可能迁移到 VLM 推理失败与证据使用的分析；但原文为纯文本 LLM 研究，未涉及 latent 状态机制。

title: GEMS-RAG: Graph-grounded Engineering Multimodal Standards Retrieval-Augmented Generation
summary: Engineering standards are challenging knowledge sources for large language models (LLMs) because they are hierarchical, multimodal, and densely connected through figures, tables, cross-references, and normative rules. Existing retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) methods often rely on unstructured text retrieval and struggle with questions requiring joint reasoning over textual provisions, visual specifications, and document structure. We propose GEMS-RAG (Graph-grounded Engineering Multimodal Standards Retrieval-Augmented Generation), a framework for grounded reasoning over engineering standards. GEMS-RAG combines hierarchical parsing, fine-grained visual entity extraction, multimodal knowledge graph construction, and graph-grounded hybrid retrieval. Instead of treating figures as monolithic images, it decomposes them into meaningful visual entities linked to textual provisions, engineering concepts, and regulatory rules. During inference, dense, sparse, and visual retrieval are combined with graph expansion to identify relevant evidence across text, figures, and document structure. We evaluate GEMS-RAG on the Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD), a large engineering standard containing egulations, technical drawings, and standardized traffic-control devices. Results show that graph-grounded multimodal retrieval improves retrieval effectiveness and question-answering performance over text-only, multimodal, and graph-based RAG baselines. Beyond MUTCD, GEMS-RAG offers a general framework for reasoning over engineering codes, technical manuals, regulatory documents, and scientific standards in safety-critical applications.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 GEMS-RAG，将工程标准文档做层次化解析，把图表拆成细粒度视觉实体并与文本条款、规则一起构建多模态知识图谱，推理时用稠密、稀疏、视觉检索结合图扩展选取证据，在 MUTCD 上评测问答效果。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「把图像拆成可链接文本条款的视觉实体」加图扩展混合检索的思路，可能为 VLM 推理中的视觉证据筛选与结构化证据组织提供可核查线索；但属文档级 RAG，未涉及 latent 状态或推理期状态生成。

title: Estimation of Propagated Risk in LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems
summary: Large Language Model (LLM) based multi-agent systems introduce a distinctive reliability challenge in which actions taken by upstream agents can affect the correctness of downstream agents. While prior work has investigated error propagation and developed methods for estimating uncertainty inherited from upstream agents, existing approaches do not explicitly model how realized sender-receiver interactions contribute to downstream error risk under different sender correctness states. In this work, we study agent-level error-risk estimation from multi-agent execution traces. We propose Interaction-Effect Propagation (IE-Prop), an interaction-conditioned model that learns separate effects for correct and incorrect upstream agents. For each sender-receiver interaction, the model combines these conditional effects using the sender's estimated error risk, and recursively propagates the resulting risk estimates through the execution graph. We evaluate our approach across three multi-agent architectures and three benchmarks. Across all evaluated architectures, our approach raises the final-node AUROC over the established baseline by approximately 0.05 points on average. Furthermore, tracking risk across multiple agent steps contributes a distinct +0.03 AUROC gain in sequential systems. These results show that realized inter-agent interactions provide predictive information beyond receiver-local evidence, while the value of multi-step risk tracking depends on the system's information-flow structure.

AI.brief_summary: 该文研究 LLM 多智能体执行轨迹中的智能体级错误风险估计，提出 IE-Prop：为上游正确的与出错的两类情形分别学习交互效应，再按发送方的估计错误风险加权合并，并沿执行图递归传播风险；在三类多智能体架构与三个基准上验证，末节点 AUROC 平均提升约 0.05。
AI.relevance_reason: 虽非视觉工作，但其「按上游正确/错误状态条件化、沿计算图递归传播风险」的思路，可能可供核查于 LVR 中多步推理状态的可靠性估计、中间步骤贡献分配与是否继续计算的判断。

title: MLIPDiff: Guiding Denoising Diffusion Models for Structure-Based Drug Design via Machine-Learned Interatomic Potentials
summary: Diffusion models have become a dominant approach to structure-based drug design. However, because they are trained primarily to fit reference structures, they often place ligands in physically implausible poses that clash with the protein. We introduce MLIPDiff, an inference-time guidance method that can be applied to pretrained diffusion models for ligand generation. The method uses physics-informed guidance from UMA (Universal Models for Atoms), a machine-learned interatomic potential (MLIP). The guidance combines four weighted energy terms (protein-ligand interaction, ligand strain, steric clash, and pocket anchoring) and uses the original model checkpoint without retraining. On CrossDocked2020, MLIPDiff completely eliminates protein-ligand collisions while preserving the ligand's local geometry, improving bond-length distributions and physical plausibility relative to the base model. Compared to models such as NucleusDiff that are specifically designed to reduce atomic clashes, MLIPDiff achieves clash-free structures without compromising local geometry. It maintains the base model's PoseBusters pass rate and attains the best median Vina Score, Vina Min, and Vina Dock, surpassing both the base model and NucleusDiff, with a median of 59.6\% of ligands per pocket binding more strongly than the reference. MLIPDiff thus addresses a limitation of prior methods by generating physically plausible structures with favorable predicted binding affinity using a single frozen model and no additional training.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 MLIPDiff：在推理阶段以机器学习原子间势 UMA 构造四项加权能量项，引导预训练扩散模型生成配体，无需重训练，在 CrossDocked2020 上消除蛋白-配体碰撞并改善键长分布与对接打分。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「冻结扩散模型＋外部能量引导」的免训练推理期约束注入方式，可能为 LVR 中沿去噪或迭代轨迹施加验证器/约束信号提供借鉴线索；但分子结构设计与视觉推理相距较远，其引导强度与几何保真的权衡是否可迁移仍需核查。

title: Augmentation-Guided Adversarial Training via Local Stability-Based Sample Selection
summary: Adversarial training remains one of the most effective defenses against adversarial attacks, but its standard PGD-based training is computationally expensive because adversarial examples are generated for every training sample. Selective adversarial training reduces this cost by perturbing only a subset of samples. However, existing selective techniques typically rely on point-wise difficulty signals such as loss, entropy, margin, or gradients. We show that these point-wise criteria do not capture local instability in a sample's neighborhood. Motivated by this, we propose Augmentation-Guided Adversarial Training (AGAT), a selective adversarial training framework that uses augmentation-induced local variation to allocate samples with unstable neighborhoods for adversarial training. AGAT ranks samples using Augmentation-based Local Stability (ALS), a lightweight score that measures the normalized change in model logits between an input and its label-preserving augmented variant. Experiments across different architectures on MNIST, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and Tiny-ImageNet-200 demonstrate that AGAT achieves comparable or higher robust accuracy while applying adversarial supervision to only 20-30% of the training samples in each minibatch. AGAT also requires less training time than all other adversarial training baselines in the computational cost evaluation.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 AGAT，用「增强诱导的局部稳定性」打分（输入与其保标签增强变体之间 logits 的归一化变化）来挑选每个 minibatch 中约 20–30% 的样本做对抗训练，在多个图像分类数据集上取得相当或更高的鲁棒精度并减少训练时间。
AI.relevance_reason: 其以邻域局部不稳定性替代 loss/entropy 等逐点信号来分配训练监督的做法，可能可供核查作为 LVR 中训练样本或推理轨迹筛选、监督贡献分配的线索；但论文只做图像分类鲁棒性，未涉及视觉-语言推理或 latent 状态本身。

title: Compression of Vision Foundation Models for Retinal OCT via Growing-Neural-Gas Codebooks and Graph-Guided Masked Image Modeling
comment: 31 pages, 2 figures, 8 tables; supplementary material provided as an ancillary file
summary: Vision foundation models for retinal imaging are large and computationally demanding, limiting point-of-care deployment. We ask how much of such a model's downstream utility survives compression into a smaller network. We propose a topology-aware discretization framework that distills a continuous foundation model into a discrete codebook, then uses it as the reconstruction target for masked image modeling (MIM). It combines gradient-free codebook learning via Growing Neural Gas, which yields an adjacency graph over the codes, with a graph-distance soft cross-entropy loss that replaces one-hot MIM targets with topologically graded supervision. With student pretraining on 383 public Duke iAMD optical coherence tomography (OCT) volumes, the pipeline distills an 86M-parameter teacher into a 22M-parameter student with at least 3.6x fewer FLOPs. The student performs close to, and in some settings above, its teacher across three classification and two segmentation benchmarks, with the magnitude and direction of the difference depending on the teacher, task, metric, and student capacity. On the external OLIVES benchmark, it surpasses its MIRAGE teacher on every metric (98.06% vs. 95.22% balanced accuracy). It works with two Vision Transformer (ViT-Base) teachers, retinal (MIRAGE) and natural-image (DINOv3); with the out-of-domain teacher, the student outperforms it on retinal-layer segmentation, indicating that the added value of retina-specific pretraining is task-dependent: largest for segmentation, while a general-domain teacher is competitive for classification. These results yield compact retinal models potentially suitable for deployment, transferring across OCT datasets, devices, and clinical tasks, including three datasets not used in the student's pretraining.

AI.brief_summary: 研究视网膜 OCT 视觉基础模型的可压缩性：用 Growing Neural Gas 学习带邻接图的离散码本，将 86M 教师蒸馏为 22M 学生，并以码本为 MIM 重建目标、用图距离软交叉熵替代 one-hot 监督，在多个分类与分割基准上接近或超过教师。

title: Detecting Temporal Concepts in Video Transformers via a No-False-Positives Test
summary: Video models have the architecture to support encoding temporal aspects of the input, i.e. concepts that require more than one frame to define, like object movement. However, because motion and appearance change are entangled, a feature that appears to encode temporal concepts like object movement may instead encode non-temporal concepts like spatial presence at different positions whose activations merely correlate with motion. To resolve this, we introduce the No-False-Positives (NFP) test, a statistical test with a formal guarantee of statistical specificity for identifying features encoding temporal concepts. Using specially designed stimuli, we apply this test to representations produced by VideoMAE, V-JEPA2, and TimeSformer, and observe that temporal features exist in each model. We validate the test first by showing it yields no temporal features for the DINOv2 image-encoder. Then, using a synthetic representation space, we show that detection rate increases with a direction's projection onto the temporal subspace, and that Sparse Autoencoder features test-flagged as temporal project much more of their norm onto the temporal subspace than unflagged features. Interventions on temporal SAE features yield mixed results across models, suggesting that intervening on temporal features may not outperform a non-temporal feature baseline.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 No-False-Positives（NFP）统计检验，以形式化特异性保证识别视频 Transformer 中真正编码时间概念（如物体运动）的特征，排除仅与运动相关的空间存在性等伪特征；在 VideoMAE、V-JEPA2、TimeSformer 上应用，以 DINOv2 作阴性对照，并对 SAE 时间特征做干预。
AI.relevance_reason: 其带假阳性控制的特征检测与 SAE 干预范式，可供核查 latent 推理状态是否真正使用视觉证据、如何区分真实编码与相关伪迹；但对象是视频表征诊断而非 VLM 推理，迁移线索仍需核查。

title: The Clustering Occupation Kernel (CLOCK) Method for Time Series Arising from Dynamical Systems
summary: We introduce the Clustering Occupation Kernel (CLOCK) method, a novel representation-based framework for clustering time series arising from dynamical systems. CLOCK embeds observed sequences into a reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS) via a time-averaged occupation kernel, enabling trajectory comparison through their RKHS norm. For systems governed by differential equations, this formulation rigorously approximates the kernel mean embedding of the invariant Sinai-Ruelle-Bowen (SRB) measure, meaning our dissimilarity metric approximates the maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) between attractors. To accommodate general time series, we introduce time lags via Takens' Embedding Theorem to reconstruct the phase space. Crucially, CLOCK natively handles trajectories of unequal lengths and irregularly-spaced observations. We validate the proposed metric using spectral clustering, demonstrating superior performance against benchmark methods on both synthetic datasets and a real-world intracranial large-scale electroencephalogram (EEG) dataset. Finally, ablation studies on the Lorenz-96 system are consistent with the theoretical convergence rates of the occupation kernels and highlight the method's strong robustness to zero-mean Gaussian noise.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 CLOCK：用时均 occupation kernel 把动力系统产生的时间序列嵌入 RKHS，以核范数作为轨迹间不相似度，并结合 Takens 时滞嵌入重构相空间，可处理不等长与不规则采样，在合成数据与 EEG 数据上用谱聚类验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 其将轨迹视为测度并嵌入 RKHS 比较的思路，可供核查用于度量长度不等、采样不齐的多步 latent 推理轨迹之间的相似性，但该文本身不涉及视觉或多模态推理。

title: Tight Learned Event-Inertial Odometry (TLEIO): a Transformer-Based Architecture for End-to-End Motion from Event Streams
summary: Event cameras provide microsecond temporal resolution, high dynamic range, and sparse asynchronous measurements, making them compelling for odometry under fast motion and challenging illumination. Yet, accurate event-based state estimation remains difficult: existing systems often use events as a complement to frames or rely on feature tracking, correspondence search, and optimization-heavy backends, limiting the efficiency promised by event sensing. We introduce Tight Learned Event-Inertial Odometry (TLEIO), a compact filter-based pipeline that learns short-window relative motion directly from voxelized event streams and tightly fuses the resulting constraints with IMU propagation. Its learned front-end, EventsFormer, predicts local displacements and per-axis uncertainty from event voxels in a single forward pass, while a stochastic-cloning EKF fuses these overlapping predictions with IMU propagation, producing metric trajectories without explicit feature tracks and pose optimization at inference time. The network is trained directly from pose displacements, without requiring event-flow labels. We evaluate TLEIO on the TartanAir/TartanEvent benchmark and on real DAVIS240c sequences. On TartanAir, TLEIO reduces average ATE from 2.26 m to 1.10 m over the IMU-only TLIO baseline, while achieving up to 48.9% lower runtime than optimization-based event odometry methods.

AI.brief_summary: TLEIO 提出紧凑的滤波式事件-惯性里程计：EventsFormer 前端从体素化事件流单次前向预测短窗相对位移与各轴不确定性，再由随机克隆 EKF 与 IMU 紧耦合，直接用位姿位移训练并在 TartanAir 与 DAVIS240c 上评测。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「一次前向同时给出运动估计与逐轴不确定性、再按不确定性加权融合」的机制，可能为 LVR 中视觉证据可靠度估计及何时采信/停止的决策提供方法线索；但事件相机里程计与多模态推理主线距离较远，需人工核查可迁移性。

title: LSTM-Style Looped Transformers with Shared KV Caches
summary: Recurrent transformers reuse weights to perform deep computation with fewer parameters. We study an LSTM-style transformer that also shares one key--value cache across its recurrent core. At width 1024, it uses 40.4% fewer parameters than an untied control at nearly matched forward FLOPs, and reduces persistent cache sets from fifteen to four. Parallel training supplies cache entries from a standard-attention pass, whereas continuation reads entries produced recursively using shared attention. We address this mismatch by aligning the two training passes' cache entries with a consistency loss during the final 10% of a fixed training-token budget. Across three model widths on FineWeb, this removes 81--89% of the continuation-loss penalty relative to full-cache evaluation. The improvement replicates on disjoint documents for two training seeds. Across four widths and 1.05--4.19B training tokens, the loss cost of weight tying is smallest at lower token budgets, suggesting an opportunity to use recurrent computation when data and model storage are limited.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究一种 LSTM 式循环 Transformer，在循环核心中共享单个 KV cache 以减少参数和持久缓存，并用一致性损失对齐并行训练与递归续写两种方式产生的 cache 条目。
AI.relevance_reason: 其跨循环共享 KV cache 及对齐并行/递归 cache 的监督方式，可能为 LVR 中循环式 latent 状态更新与「缓存如何影响 latent 相似度」的分析提供线索，但纯文本设定下可迁移性尚待核查。

title: Multiple Importance Sampling for Guided Speculative Inference
comment: 9 pages, 1 figure. Presented at the IEEE ISIT 2026 Workshop on Information Theory for Large Language Models (IT4LLM)
summary: We study an extension of the Guided Speculative Inference (GSI) algorithm for test-time-scaling of large language models (LLMs) to a novel setting where an ensemble of smaller LLMs proposes draft reasoning steps which are later verified by a larger base model and a process reward model. Using the established framework of multiple importance sampling (MIS), we introduce weighting schemes to aggregate samples from a diverse collection of proposal distributions. We provide new bounds on the KL divergence from the optimal reward-tilted target distribution and the expected reward degradation, then demonstrate that the well-known balance heuristic is optimal. Compared to GSI with a single well-tuned drafter, combining several diverse LLMs while retaining the same total number of samples maintains competitive pass-at-$N$ downstream performance while being mathematically robust to situations where the support of a single draft model does not cover that of the target, where GSI may fail.

AI.brief_summary: 该文将 Guided Speculative Inference 扩展到由多个小模型集成起草推理步骤、再由大模型与过程奖励模型验证的设定，用多重要性采样框架提出样本加权方案，给出到奖励倾斜目标分布的 KL 界与期望奖励退化界，并证明 balance heuristic 最优。
AI.relevance_reason: 纯文本 test-time scaling 工作，但其对多个提议分布的加权聚合、验证器打分与奖励倾斜目标的理论分析，可供核查是否迁移到多路 latent 假设的合并与贡献分配；与视觉证据筛选无直接联系。

title: One Call Ahead: Packed Self-Speculative Decoding with Diffusion Drafting
summary: Autoregressive (AR) language models generate tokens sequentially, so generating long outputs is costly. Speculative decoding mitigates this by using a lightweight drafter to propose multiple tokens for the target AR model to verify in parallel, while a diffusion-based drafter can produce an entire draft block in one forward pass. In models with AR and diffusion modes, one network both drafts and verifies, but drafting still waits for verification, so the standard schedule needs two sequential model calls per iteration. Existing one-call schedules avoid the wait but incur input size quadratic in the speculative width. Motivated by this efficiency bottleneck, we introduce Packed-SS, a self-speculative decoding schedule that verifies and drafts in a single model call with input size linear in the speculative width, while preserving the target model's distribution. The key idea is to let the diffusion drafter run one call ahead: while verifying the current draft, the model simultaneously constructs the next draft from an older verified prefix and keeps its unresolved suffix for the next iteration. Under a mild monotonicity assumption on the drafter, we further show that Packed-SS requires no more model calls than the standard two-call decoding in the greedy setting. Experiments on Nemotron 3B/8B and SetDLM 1.7B show higher throughput and lower mean wall time than both baselines under greedy decoding.

AI.brief_summary: 论文针对同时具备 AR 与 diffusion 模式的模型提出 Packed-SS 推测解码调度：让扩散草稿器「提前一次调用」运行，在验证当前草稿的同一次前向中基于较早的已验证前缀构造下一份草稿并保留未解析后缀，使输入规模随推测宽度线性增长，并在贪心解码下证明调用次数不多于标准两调用方案。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「单次调用内并行完成生成与验证、跨迭代携带未解析后缀」的流水线式状态更新，可能为 LVR 中潜在推理状态的增量生成、草稿—验证交替与动态停止调度提供方法线索，但线性打包是否能适用于视觉或 latent token 需核查。

title: How To Build A Modern Diffusion Language Model
summary: The frontier of large language model (LLM) performance has advanced rapidly in recent years, fueled by scaling laws for pretraining on large text corpora. However, mainstream LLMs have fundamental limitations: they generate text autoregressively, producing outputs sequentially from left to right one token at a time. This sequential process leaves parallel GPU hardware underutilized during inference--a bottleneck that has grown acute as progress shifts toward scaling post-training and inference-time compute--and commits irreversibly to each token without the ability to revise earlier mistakes. Discrete diffusion models address these limitations by generating tokens in parallel, starting from a noisy or masked sequence and iteratively refining the entire output over a series of denoising steps. This parallel generative process enables speeds of thousands of tokens per second, provides a new axis of inference-time compute scaling, and supports built-in error correction and controllable generation. Over the past two years, discrete diffusion has scaled to billions of parameters across biological sequence modeling and natural language, with open-weights and commercial releases from leading labs. This article provides a survey of key ideas in discrete diffusion and a high-level introduction to how modern diffusion LLMs are built, covering their foundations, core algorithmic and architectural building blocks, applications in biology and language, and implications for future LLM scaling laws.

AI.brief_summary: 这是一篇关于离散扩散语言模型的综述，梳理其基本原理、核心算法与架构组件、在生物序列与自然语言上的应用，并讨论并行生成与推理期计算对 LLM 规模扩展的影响。
AI.relevance_reason: 论文虽为纯文本综述，但其对并行去噪、迭代精修与错误校正的整理，可能为 LVR 中 parallel/loop 式推理状态的生成与更新提供方法线索，值得核查是否可用于多步视觉推理。

title: Rethinking Microscopy Generation: Co-Designed Diffusion for Biologically Interpretable Single-Cell Synthesis
summary: Generative models for microscopy can already produce realistic whole-image fields of view, but offer no principled way to control how each individual cell looks. We address this gap by recasting microscopy generation at the single-cell level and designing the input controls and the model's internal representation jointly, so that both are organized along the same biologically meaningful directions. On the input side, we aggregate a long list of standard cell measurements into a small set of semantic axes (size, elongation, brightness, texture, etc.) that are each named, measurable, and traversable. On the model side, we introduce BioVAE, an encoder-decoder whose latent space is explicitly aligned with the same set of measurements. A key finding is that the benefit of biologically structuring the latent emerges only when conditioning is also moved to the semantic axes, showing that the two ends must be designed jointly. Experiments on LIVECell show that semantic-axis conditioning substantially improves generative fidelity over high-dimensional conditioning, a blind study with biologists confirms the realism of generated cells, and per-axis traversals produce stable and interpretable phenotypic changes.

AI.brief_summary: 论文将显微图像生成细化到单细胞层面，把细胞测量聚合成可遍历的语义轴，并设计 latent space 与这些轴对齐的 BioVAE，联合设计条件输入与内部表示以提升生成保真度和可解释性。
